title: Write inside Connector.WithTransaction blocks: rollback on throw, returned values, SubTransaction savepoints
task: Make a change to a Revit document safely with the connector: read at top level, write inside Connector.WithTransaction(doc, () => {...}), get a value back from the block, rely on a throwing body being rolled back even when the script catches, and use a native SubTransaction as a savepoint inside a block. Connector transaction model; error codes script-write-outside-transaction and script-subtransaction-needs-transaction.

pitfalls.symptom: `script-write-outside-transaction` (Attempt to modify the model outside of transaction) on a Level.Create, parameter Set or Delete at the top of the script.
pitfalls.cause: Since #146 the connector opens no transaction by default; the document is readable but not modifiable outside a Connector.WithTransaction block.
pitfalls.fix: Wrap the write in Connector.WithTransaction(doc, () => { ... }); reads stay outside. One block per batch of related writes.

pitfalls.symptom: Work from a block whose body threw is missing even though the script caught the exception and continued.
pitfalls.cause: WithTransaction rolls the block back on any exception before rethrowing; catching it does not restore the writes.
pitfalls.fix: Expected. Put the fallback writes in a NEW block after the catch; the document stays fully writable.

pitfalls.cause: A SubTransaction needs an open transaction, and none is open outside a WithTransaction block.
pitfalls.fix: Start the SubTransaction inside a WithTransaction block, always in a `using`; Dispose without Commit rolls its slice back.

pitfalls.symptom: `script-api-denied`: constructing Transaction, TransactionGroup, or a SubTransaction outside a `using`.
pitfalls.cause: Own transactions break the one-open-transaction-per-document invariant the connector relies on; a non-`using` SubTransaction left open at block end destabilised Revit (crash observed).
pitfalls.fix: Never construct Transaction/TransactionGroup; SubTransaction only as `using (var st = new SubTransaction(doc))`.
